_why: ONE TABLE, TWO READERS. gate.py runs the checks in the cloud and check.js
runs them here, and both have to agree about which check a change can
break. Written twice they drift, and the one that drifts is the one that
stops running - so it is written once, here, and consistency.js fails if
it stops covering every harness or every gate step.
BZ, 2026-10-01: 'Every cycle all of them have to run even if we only
changed one page. We need a better, more streamlined method.' Measured
the same day: the sixteen local checks are 203 seconds and browser.js and
sync.js are 123 of them, paid on every change including one that moved a
`reaches` is what a check can be broken BY. A check appears under every
kind of change that can break it, never under the one that usually does.
`secs` was measured on BZ's PC on 2026-10-01 and is here so a change to
this table is made with its price in view.
ALWAYS means exactly that: run it whatever changed. They are the cheap
ones that notice structural damage - something undefined, a rule written
twice, a named lock that no longer matches the file it names.

kinds.engine: index.html above the STATE + RENDER banner
kinds.harness: a check's own file - it runs itself

checks.name: audit
checks.note: the named lock matches index.html, and it runs consistency and screens itself unless the gate says it has them

checks.name: appsscript
checks.note: engine too: L.GS_BUILD and the service's build must move together

checks.name: rules
checks.note: needs Java, so it runs in the cloud gate only
